sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: h1 (notes/hooks.md), sketch i01. Medium target, Hard welcome (user 2026-10-10: "there is
  no slot for Easy Tier for this bundle, we should target medium and high"). Shape follows the workspace's
  measured Medium recipe 3 (one scenario, several independent document-grounded steps, asked as one total);
  that is a design note, not a prediction. Measured platform result pending.
- Dependency plan: D07 (EPA, April 24, 2026, proposed SNURs for two cathode oxides): reclaiming the oxide is
  processing; doing it with dust controls under 99% is a significant new use (L320), which needs a SNUN (L101);
  a SNUN costs a large business an estimated $45,496, fee included (L70); each destination country needs one
  export notice at about $106 (L71). D04 (DOE final FEOC interpretation, May 6, 2024) decides the three
  prospects: Polish firm, 50% held by a Chinese city, is a FEOC (L308, L323); Indonesian subsidiary of a private
  Shanghai company is not (L236, also L123-124, L257); Japanese firm is not, because the province's two of
  five seats count at their 20% of board voting power (L138), below 25%. Two notices: 106 + 106 = 212.
  45,496 + 212 = 45,708.
- Universe: three prospects, all named in the question. Excluded: Poland (FEOC by control). Included:
  Indonesia, Japan. Decoy: the Polish firm, a foreign-incorporated company that a jurisdiction-only reading keeps.
- Necessity: D07 -> the SNUN cost, the export-notice cost and the 99% trigger. Grep of all seven texts: "SNUN",
  "SNUR", "export notification" and "$45,496" occur in D07 only; D06 is a TSCA petition decision without costs.
  Without D07 no amount exists, and the figure is from an April 2026 notice. D04 -> the board-seat valuation
  (L138), printed in D04 only ("voting power on the board": one hit in the bundle). D02, the proposal, prints
  "25% or more of the entity's board seats" (L110) and nothing on valuing a seat, so with D02 in place of D04
  two of five seats is 40%, the Japanese firm is a FEOC and the total is $45,602. D02 also carries the
  subnational-government and jurisdiction-subsidiary rules (L95, L166), which is why it is not ticked and why
  one prospect rests on a D04-only clarification. D05 only points to the FEOC definition. Optional removal
  probe without Doc 4 (rev 0, recorded under Blind solve): the solver took D02's seat count and answered
  $45,602, forced guess $45,602 at p 0.85, so the gold was not reached without Doc 4.
- Selected-lever checks: Match, then exclude: without the FEOC exclusion all three countries are notified,
  45,496 + 106 + 106 + 106 = 45,814. Same series, right edition: the proposal's text (D02 L110) gives $45,602.
  Calculate across documents: no decoy needed.
- Targeted failure modes: (1) Look-alike measure: seat share 2 / 5 = 40% taken for board voting power (20%);
  Japanese firm dropped; 45,496 + 106 = 45,602. Set by D04's operative sentence (L323, "board seats") against
  its comment response (L138), and by D02 L110. (2) Wrong jurisdiction or scope: the Shanghai parent is a FEOC
  by jurisdiction (L317) and that status is carried to its Indonesian subsidiary against L236; Indonesian firm dropped;
  45,602. Both errors: 45,496. Considered and not declared: Polish firm kept (45,814), because a 50% government
  holding is plain under L323; export notices only (212) or with the Polish firm (318), a slip the wording
  "notifying EPA ... altogether" rules out since D07 uses "notify EPA" for the SNUN (L25, L245) and "notice to
  EPA" for exports (L71); user fee added again, 45,496 + 37,000 + 212 = 82,708, ruled out by L70's "These
  estimates include ... the payment of a user fee"; small-business figure, 14,976 + 212 = 15,188, ruled out by
  "large". Offer to align the declared modes with a run's observed wrong answers before Submit.
- Calculation verification: script (scratchpad quotes.py, 2026-10-10): 45496 + 106 + 106 = 45708; wrong routes
  45602, 45814, 82708, 15188. Units: U.S. dollars, estimates as printed ("an estimated", "approximately"); no
  rounding, no sign. Second route: 106 x 2 = 212, 212 + 45496 = 45708.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: the capture's overview lists "$45,496 per SNUN submission for large businesses"
  and "$106 estimated cost per export notification" under Doc 7 and "25% FEOC threshold for control of an
  entity" under Doc 4; it states neither the board-seat rule nor any total. "45,708" and "45,602" occur
  nowhere in the bundle or the capture. Shortest complete route found: the eight steps above.
- Precision/readings: (a) timing: export notices already apply to a proposed SNUR (D07 L62, L131) but the SNUN
  duty starts when the rule is final (L53 "if finalized as proposed"), so the question says "once ... final".
  (b) "a covered oxide": D07 proposes two sections under one generic name (L300-304); one oxide means one SNUN
  and one notice per country. (c) "notifying EPA" spans both notice types (see above). (d) the large-business
  SNUN cost is printed once; the small-business cost is printed as $14,976 (L70) and $14,967 (L249), which is
  why the recycler is "large". (e) D04 L150 says a 50-50 joint venture with a FEOC member is a FEOC; no
  prospect is a joint venture or a tiered minority chain, so that sentence and scenario 3 are not engaged.
  (f) "private" for the Shanghai company follows D04 L125 ("privately held with no formal control by the
  government"). (g) board votes are not the owners' "voting rights" (D04 L134), and the province holds no
  stated equity, so 20% is the highest metric for the Japanese firm.
- Completeness: complete capture, no gaps (intake.json: 7 of 7 documents, matches_capture true). All seven
  documents read in full (D03 by the mapper only; not used).
- Style/set review: one ask, 59 words by whitespace count (hyphenated compounds counted once); a scenario, so
  longer than the 12-20 word aim, kept under the form's 60-word warning. First question on this bundle.
- Revision history: rev 0 said "Korean subsidiary". The removal probe listed a reading of "Korean" as North
  Korean, a covered nation in D04, which would make that subsidiary a FEOC by jurisdiction ($45,496). Rev 1
  names Indonesia instead; nothing else changed. One focused repair for one observed reading.
- Optional diagnostics (concrete issues: one parse of a dense scenario; whether D02 can replace D04), rev 0
  only, not rerun for the country change: blind solve on all seven documents matched $45,708 with high
  confidence, minimal documents D07 and D04, and said D02 "cannot replace D04"; it named $45,602, $212 and
  $45,814 as rejected readings. These are fairness checks, not tier evidence.
- Warnings answered: origin claude is the actual writer (export takes user only). Form-numbers: 99% (Doc 7,
  character 26,471, inside an evidence quote) is printed past the floor's stale bound of 19,581; the live form
  passed printed inputs at characters 43,740 to 50,854 on 2026-10-09 (aq-02486), so no flag is expected. If
  the form does flag it, the fallback for Step 1 is "dust controls that meet the proposal's minimum capture
  and control efficiency". Steps 4 and 6 give the scenario's shares in words ("half", "a fifth") so that no
  scenario digit has to be found deep in Doc 4. The two rev 0 diagnostic records are kept as history; the
  first rev 1 snapshot (523246865cc9...) was superseded untested by this wording change to Steps 4 and 6.

sections.question: Once EPA's 2026 significant-new-use proposal is final, a large recycler reclaims a covered oxide with 90%-efficient dust controls, exporting to non-FEOC prospects among: a Chinese city's 50%-owned Polish firm; a private Shanghai company's Indonesian subsidiary; a Japanese firm where a Chinese province picks two of five directors, casting 20% of board votes. What would notifying EPA cost it altogether?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 7, proposed significant new uses): it is a significant new use to process the substance, where processing includes recycling or reclaiming it from batteries, except with dust controls of a minimum capture and control efficiency of 99%, and a SNUN is required prior to any significant new use. The recycler's 90% controls are below that minimum, so it must notify EPA with a SNUN.

Step 2. Source input (Doc 7, estimated costs for SNUN submissions): a SNUN submission costs an estimated $45,496 for large business submitters. The estimate already includes preparing and submitting the SNUN and the user fee.

Step 3. Source input (Doc 7, estimated costs for export notifications): a person exporting a substance that is the subject of a SNUR gives EPA a one-time notice for the first export to a particular country, at approximately $106 per notification.

Step 4. Source input (Doc 4, final interpretation, government and control tests): a government of a foreign country includes a subnational government, and an entity is controlled when 25% or more of its board seats, voting rights or equity interest, each metric evaluated independently, is held by that government. A Chinese city holds half of the Polish firm, above that threshold, so that firm is an FEOC and receives no export.

Step 5. Source input (Doc 4, explanation of the jurisdiction test): a company with its principal place of business in a covered nation is an FEOC by jurisdiction, but subsidiaries of such an FEOC are not automatically FEOCs on that ground. A subsidiary is one only if it is itself subject to the covered nation's jurisdiction or controlled by its government. The Indonesian subsidiary of a private Shanghai company is neither, so it is not an FEOC.

Step 6. Source input (Doc 4, response to comments on board seats): DOE values a board seat at its voting power on the board. The province's directors cast only a fifth of board votes, which is below 25%, so the Japanese firm is not an FEOC, although they fill two of five seats.

Step 7. Calculation (Doc 7): export notices for the two allowed destination countries, Indonesia and Japan, in dollars: 106 + 106 = 212.

Step 8. Final answer (Doc 7 and Doc 4): total cost of notifying EPA, in dollars: 45,496 + 212 = 45,708.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Look-alike measure
How a careless solver fails: Takes the wrong line item

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

Why these are traps: Look-alike measure: Doc 4's control test names board seats, and two of five looks like 40%; its comment response values a seat by board voting power, 20%. Wrong jurisdiction or scope: the Shanghai parent's status is carried to its Indonesian subsidiary. Either drops one country: $45,602, not $45,708.
